content: {"rules": ["Forecast models consistently underestimate price movements in the short term, especially after bullish sentiment spikes.", "Sentiment indicators show strong negative bias when supply net is high, suggesting model overconfidence in upward trends.", "Price corrections often occur after consecutive bullish sentiment events, indicating sentiment-driven mean reversion.", "Model forecasts exhibit lagging behavior, with price turning points appearing 3–5 days after sentiment shifts.", "High supply net events correlate with downward price pressure, requiring model adjustments to account for supply shocks.", "Sentiment and price movements diverge during high supply periods, suggesting sentiment is not a reliable predictor of price direction.", "Forecast accuracy improves when sentiment aligns with recent price trends, indicating sentiment interaction with price momentum.", "Models should incorporate event-driven supply adjustments to avoid persistent forecast bias during auction cycles."]}
